snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹40 lakh–1.5 crore for automatic grinding, blending and packing lines
snapshot.margin_d2c: 40–55% gross margin selling your own brand online
snapshot.margin_production: 15–25% selling in bulk to hotels, caterers and retailers
snapshot.distribution_note: Local retail and bulk buyers are steady; national brands dominate shelves

tailwinds: Buyers worry about adulteration and pay more for pure, traceable spices.
India is the world's biggest spice producer, and many districts are ODOP spice clusters.
PMFME subsidies support small food-processing units.
Regional blends and single-origin spices sell well online and abroad.
headwinds: MDH, Everest and other big brands dominate retail shelves.
Spice export controversies over pesticide and contamination have increased testing.
Raw spice prices swing with harvests.
Grinding heat can reduce flavour unless you invest in better machines.
angle_2026: Recent contamination controversies have made buyers and exporters far more careful about spice quality. In 2026, small spice brands grow by proving purity with lab tests, sourcing directly from farmers in known growing regions, and selling fresh, small-batch or cold-ground spices.
cost_basis: Estimated for a small unit grinding and packing spices for retail and bulk buyers, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: FSSAI licence, pesticide and adulteration tests

What share of sales is repeat?

bootstrap_takeaway: Start by buying directly from farmers or mandis in a spice-growing region, sell pure, tested spices to local shops and online, and add bulk sales to restaurants.
sourcing_edge: Buying spices directly from growers in clusters such as Guntur (chilli), Erode (turmeric), Unjha (cumin) and Kerala (pepper and cardamom) at harvest gives you better quality and prices.

hard_truths.title: Big brands own shelves
hard_truths.text: Retail shelves are dominated by national brands. Build your brand online and through local shops first.

hard_truths.title: Quality testing
hard_truths.text: Pesticide residues and contamination must be tested. One bad batch can end export or retail deals.

hard_truths.title: Price swings
hard_truths.text: Chilli, turmeric and cardamom prices swing widely. Buy at harvest and store carefully.

hard_truths.title: Moisture and pests
hard_truths.text: Poor storage ruins stock. Invest in clean, dry storage.

plan_goal: The aim is ₹1.5 lakh in sales, with at least 10 repeat buyers.

plan.title: Source and test
steps: Visit a spice-growing region and meet farmers or traders.
Buy samples and test them in a lab.

plan.title: Set up
steps: Get FSSAI licence and set up grinding.

plan.title: Sell
steps: Sell to 20 local shops and 5 restaurants.

plan.title: Review the numbers
steps: Decide on bulk or retail focus.
